b: The races · 17, 37 and 54 KM - It's up to you. The 17 KM* to discover, the 37 KM** to push yourself, the 54 KM*** to go all in. Comparison The three formats at a glance. Sunday 4 April 2027, start and finish at the Village LIGHT ON in Celles-sur-Plaine. Same lake, three ways to loop around it. t: Weekend programme and Village LIGHT ON · Trail Pierre-Percée 2027
d: Bib pick-up on Saturday 3 April, starts on Sunday 4 April 2027 from 7:30: the hour-by-hour programme, the Village LIGHT ON and Lake Pierre-Percée.
h: Programme & Village LIGHT ON - A weekend by the lake.
The lake, the forest, the ridges
It all happens at the Village LIGHT ON.
b: Programme & Village LIGHT ON - A weekend by the lake. Saturday for the bibs, Sunday for the running, and the Village LIGHT ON in the middle of it all. The LIGHT ON universe The LIGHT ON spirit. Serious trail, without taking ourselves seriously. That's the idea. There's a distance for you First bib or trail regular: 17, 37 or 54 KM. And everyone meets again at the same finish aid station. The lake, the forest, the ridges Forests, ridges and lakeshore: the routes go where the massif is at its finest. Remember to look up between two climbs. Everyone's in the race Runners, volunteers, supporters by the trail: everyone is part of the adventure. And the more of us there are, the more the smiles multiply. We love that! "The trail atmosphere was well captured. Very friendly and open to everyone." - Paul R. 17 KM* Fun before the clock We come for the kilometres and the finish line... but also to look up and get an eyeful! "The route was really lovely, varied and pretty well balanced in terms of difficulty." - Benjamin B. 17 KM* Sorted, no fuss Markings, aid stations, marshals, bibs: it's all ready, and the good mood comes included. All you have to do is run. "Great spirit, very pleasant route, volunteers really on hand, everything was simple." - Emilie R. 17 KM* Programme The weekend, hour by hour. Saturday to settle in, Sunday to run. The 54 starts first, the 17 brings up the rear. Saturday 3 April - Race eve 17:00 - Village LIGHT ON opens & bib pick-up Bib pick-up from 17:00 to 19:00 and partner stands. Sunday 4 April - Race day 06:00 - Bib pick-up Village LIGHT ON opens and welcomes runners, from 06:00 to 09:00. 07:30 - Start · 54 KM*** The longest format gets things going. 08:30 - Start · 37 KM** The 37 takes over. 09:30 - Start · 17 KM* The 17 closes out the starts. 12:00 - Prize-giving Podiums and a few last cheers before heading home. Village LIGHT ON It all happens at the Village LIGHT ON. Start, finish, final aid station, stands and refreshments: it's all in one place, in Celles-sur-Plaine. Stands & partners Partners and the players of the Pays des Lacs set up their stands at the Village LIGHT ON, from bib pick-up through to the podiums. Food on site Refreshments and food made with local produce on Sunday. For the coffee before and the drink after. LIGHT ON Shop The LIGHT ON shop sets up at the Village. Something to take home from the race, on top of the medal. LIGHT ON Kids A space for the youngest, with a bouncy castle weather permitting. The grown-ups run, the little ones bounce. LIGHT OFF The zone to unplug: deckchairs by the lake, before or after the race. Family and friends cheer at the finish, enjoy the lake and save a spot in the sun for those still out there. Prize-giving Sunday at midday, at the Village LIGHT ON: podiums, applause, and a "see you next year". Pierre-Percée & the Pays des Lacs Lake Pierre-Percée. Start and finish in Celles-sur-Plaine (Vosges, 88110), by Lake de la Plaine. Just to the north, on the Meurthe-et-Moselle side, one of the largest lakes in Lorraine and miles of forest: it's Lake Pierre-Percée that sets the tone for the routes. The lake One of the largest lakes in Lorraine, in Meurthe-et-Moselle, just north of the Village LIGHT ON. The routes run alongside it, above it, and everyone meets it again at the finish. The Vosges forest Firs, undergrowth, ridges and singletrack: you run at the heart of the massif. For the detail of the three tracks, head to the 17, 37 and 54 KM routes. Getting there and staying over About 1h10 from Nancy, 1h20 from Strasbourg and 1h from Épinal. Access, parking and accommodation around the lake: it's all in the practical info. Eco-responsibility Running without leaving a trace. We run in the Pierre-Percée massif one Sunday a year. The rest of the time it belongs to those who live here: we leave it as we found it. Zero waste on the trails Reusable cups at the aid stations and systematic sorting. Carrying your own eco-cup is encouraged on every route. Respectful routes Existing trails and non-permanent markings. Everything is taken down after the race to leave nothing behind in the massif. Short-supply aid stations Local, seasonal produce wherever possible, to limit the footprint and support the region's producers. Shared travel Carpooling encouraged between runners to reduce the impact of journeys to the lake. All that's missing is you. Registration is open. See you on 4 April 2027. Register

b: Plan your visit · practical info - Everything to reach the start line. Bibs, start times, kit, aid stations, safety: everything you need to know before the start. The rest is your legs. Registration Register for the race. Registration for the LIGHT ON TRAIL Pierre-Percée*** 2027 is open, online and within the limit of available bibs. Here's the essentials before you confirm yours. "Great organisation, easy to pick up the bibs, friendly and helpful volunteers, lovely route… I'll be back!" Victor D. 17 KM* Registration Open since 29 September for the 17 KM*, the 37 KM** and the 54 KM***. Limited number of bibs: it's best to register early. Licence & health For adults: an FFA licence (Athlé Compétition, Entreprise or Running), a Pass' J'aime Courir or a PPS certificate (Parcours de Prévention Santé, done online). To be uploaded to njuko no later than two weeks before the race. Minors: see the rules. Bib pick-up At the Village LIGHT ON, on Saturday from 17:00 to 19:00 and on Sunday from 06:00 to 09:00, in Celles-sur-Plaine. Bibs are not posted out. Prices and registration: it all happens on njuko. A question? Access & parking Reaching the lake. Start and finish at the Village LIGHT ON, at the Base de Loisirs de Celles-sur-Plaine (Vosges, 88110), by Lake de la Plaine, a few minutes from Lake Pierre-Percée. "Really lovely route. Easy to get to. Thank you all for this great organisation! See you next year without a doubt!" Eric M. 17 KM* By car Village LIGHT ON in Celles-sur-Plaine: about 1h10 from Nancy, 1h20 from Strasbourg and 1h from Épinal. Directions to the Village LIGHT ON. Parking Signposted parking near the Village LIGHT ON. Follow the signage and the volunteers' instructions on arrival for a smooth access. Carpooling We encourage carpooling between runners to limit the impact of journeys and make parking easier around the lake. Accommodation Why not stay for the weekend ? The lake and the forest are well worth a night on site. And your legs will thank you for not getting straight back in the car. Where to stay By the lake, in Celles-sur-Plaine like the Village LIGHT ON: the lake cottages and the Pierre-Percée Pays des Lacs campsite. In the surrounding villages, other accommodation, gîtes and guesthouses. Discover the area Canoeing, paddle, treetop adventure, leisure park: the Pierre-Percée Pays des Lacs site lists the activities around the lake, plenty to extend the weekend. Book early To sleep by the lake, it's best to get in early. The simplest way: book the same day as your bib. Food Eating on site. At the Village LIGHT ON or nearby, something to eat before… and above all after. At the Village LIGHT ON Refreshments and food made with local produce on Sunday. Aid stations Drinks and food aid stations on the routes, a full aid station at the finish, short-supply and zero-waste. Nearby Shops and restaurants in the neighbouring villages round out the offer for the rest of the weekend. Runner tips Line up with a clear head. Start times, kit, aid stations, markings and safety. This information will be refined over the coming weeks. Start times 54 KM***: start at 07:30. 37 KM**: start at 08:30. 17 KM*: start at 09:30. All starts are from the Village LIGHT ON, in Celles-sur-Plaine. Kit Semi-self-sufficient races: a personal water supply is strongly recommended, as well as trail shoes. Remember to bring 4 safety pins or a bib holder too. Canicross not allowed. Aid stations 17 KM*: a drinks aid station around km 11. 37 KM**: drinks and food at km 11 and km 26. 54 KM***: drinks and food spread across the whole distance. Full aid station at the finish, local produce and zero-waste. Markings Routes marked with signs, flags and removable ground marking, taken down after the race. Volunteer marshals at the key points and junctions. "The route was top and well marked." - Sophie C. 37 KM** Safety & first aid First-aid posts, a medical team and marshals across the whole setup. Cut-off times: km 11.3 at 2h15 (17 KM* and 37 KM**) and km 26.2 at 4h45 (37 KM**). For the 54 KM*** (start 7:30): km 11.3 at 2h15, km 28.3 at 5h30, km 43.4 at 8h30, finish within 10h30 maximum. Rules & roadbook The full rules are online. The roadbook for each route (profiles, aid stations, cut-off times) is coming soon. A question in the meantime? Write to us. FAQ Frequently asked questions. Do I need a licence to take part? No, but you do need proof. For adults: an FFA licence (Athlé Compétition, Entreprise or Running), a Pass' J'aime Courir or a PPS certificate, to be uploaded to njuko no later than two weeks before the race. Conditions for minors are in the rules. What is the minimum age? 17 KM*: from the Junior category (born in 2009 or earlier). 37 KM** and 54 KM***: from the Espoir category (born in 2007 or earlier). Can I register on the day? No, registration is online only, on njuko. It closes on Thursday 1 April 2027 at 8:00 pm, or earlier if all the bibs have gone. I can no longer come, what should I do? You can transfer your bib to another runner until Thursday 1 April 2027 at 8:00 pm, from your njuko participant area ("Transfer my registration"). With a medical certificate, 50% of the registration fee is refunded up to one month before the race. It's all detailed in the rules. Are the races timed? Yes, all three distances are timed. The spirit stays friendly above all: we come for the kilometres and the finish line... but also to look up and get an eyeful! Is there a finisher medal and a gift? Yes! Every participant gets a tee-shirt as a gift, and on the 17, the 37 and the 54, every finisher leaves with their medal, right after the finish line. "The little medal at the finish is really great. Better than any other gift." - Hervé G. 37 KM** Can I run with my dog? No, canicross is not allowed on the routes, for the safety of runners and out of respect for the massif. Are there cut-off times? Yes: km 11.3 at 2h15 (17 KM* and 37 KM**) and km 26.2 at 4h45 (37 KM**). For the 54 KM*** (start 7:30): km 11.3 at 2h15, km 28.3 at 5h30, km 43.4 at 8h30, finish within 10h30 maximum. What should I bring? Semi-self-sufficient races: a personal water supply and trail shoes are strongly recommended. And for the bib: 4 safety pins or a bib holder. Another question? Write to us at hello@lightontri.com or call +33 3 74 47 56 52. We'll get back to you. A question before you register ? Write to us, we'll reply. Registration is open. Register Write to us

d: Rules of the LIGHT ON TRAIL Pierre-Percée*** 2027: races, categories, registration, medical certificate or PPS, equipment, aid stations, cut-off times, refunds.
h: Article 16 · Image rights and personal data
b: 2027 rules - The rules. Everything you need to know before the start. By registering, you accept these rules: take five minutes to read them. Article 1 · Races The LIGHT ON TRAIL event for the 2027 season is: LIGHT ON TRAIL Pierre-Percée***, Sunday 4 April 2027. Taking part implies knowledge and acceptance of these rules. By registering, the competitor gives the organisation express permission to use any still or audiovisual images in which they may appear during the event, on any medium, including promotional and/or advertising material. Article 2 · Distances and categories Trail 17 KM*: open to all, licensed or not, from the Junior category (born in 2009 or earlier). Trail 37 KM**: open to all, licensed or not, from the Espoir category (born in 2007 or earlier). Trail 54 KM***: open to all, licensed or not, from the Espoir category (born in 2007 or earlier). Start and finish of each format: Base de Loisirs, 88110 Celles-sur-Plaine. Every participant agrees to follow the course in full. Article 3 · Registration Registration is online only, on njuko. No registration on site. Trail 17 KM*: €19 Trail 37 KM**: €39 Trail 54 KM***: €49 Registration closes on Thursday 1 April 2027 at 20:00, subject to available race numbers. A waiting list may be set up. Certificate, licence or PPS To be valid, every registration must be accompanied by one of the supporting documents below. Adults: an Athlé Compétition, Athlé Entreprise or Athlé Running licence issued by the FFA, or a "Pass' J'aime Courir" issued by the FFA and completed by a doctor, valid on the date of the event (FFA Santé and Encadrement licences are not accepted); or a certificate (paper, electronic or QR code) stating that the person has completed the Parcours de Prévention Santé (PPS) set up by the FFA on its dedicated platform. Minors: an Athlé Compétition, Athlé Entreprise or Athlé Running licence issued by the FFA, or a "Pass' J'aime Courir" completed by a doctor, valid on the date of the event (FFA Santé, Encadrement and Découverte licences are not accepted); or a valid sports licence, mentioning no contraindication to the practice of sport, athletics or competitive running, issued by a federation partnered with the FFA: FCD, FFSA, FFH, FSPN, Fédération sportive des ASPTT, FSCF, FSGT, UFOLEP; and, in all cases, a health questionnaire filled in jointly by the athlete and the persons holding parental authority. If any section calls for a positive answer, a medical certificate of no contraindication less than six months old is required. Supporting documents must be uploaded to the registration site no later than two weeks before the event to finally validate the registration. Runner's commitments By registering, each runner: declares having read the rules and the ethics of the race, and agrees to comply with them in every respect; declares holding individual accident insurance covering rescue, search and evacuation costs in France; declares having checked the medical contraindications that might concern them and releases the organisation from any medical problem arising during the event due to negligence on their part. Every entry is personal. Anyone handing over their race number without going through the official transfer (article 13) will be held responsible in the event of an accident suffered or caused by the bearer of the race number. Any race number obtained in breach of these rules may lead to disqualification. The race number must be fully legible during the race. Article 4 · Race number collection At the Village LIGHT ON, in Celles-sur-Plaine: on Saturday 3 April 2027 from 17:00 to 19:00, and on Sunday 4 April 2027 from 6:00 to 9:00. Race numbers are not sent by post. Article 5 · Programme for Sunday 4 April 2027 6:00 - 9:00: race number collection 7:30: start of the Trail 54 KM*** 8:30: start of the Trail 37 KM** 9:30: start of the Trail 17 KM* 12:00: awards ceremony Article 6 · Equipment Each participant dresses according to the weather. Trail shoes are strongly recommended. The trail is run in semi-autonomy: a personal water supply is strongly recommended. Canicross is not allowed. Article 7 · Course and marking The three races are marked loops, with signs, flags and an erasable ground marking that protects the environment. All the marking is removed after the race. Article 8 · Safety and medical assistance Safety is provided by marshals put in place by the organisation, who watch over the safety of competitors and the smooth running of the event. Medical assistance is provided by a professional medical team. Each participant must report a runner in distress to the medical assistance or to the marshals. Article 9 · Aid stations The trail is a semi-autonomy race. Trail 17 KM*: one liquid aid station at km 11. Trail 37 KM**: one liquid and solid aid station at km 11 and at km 26. Trail 54 KM***: liquid and solid aid stations spread along the course, detailed with the track. A full aid station awaits all runners at the finish. Article 10 · Cut-off times 2h15 at km 11.3 for the Trail 17 KM* and the Trail 37 KM**. 4h45 at km 26.2 (Col de la Chapelotte, on the way back) for the Trail 37 KM**. For the Trail 54 KM*** (start 07:30): 2h15 at km 11.3 (09:45), 5h30 at km 28.3 (13:00), 8h30 at km 43.4 (16:00), and finish within 10h30 maximum (18:00). Article 11 · Rankings and awards Every finisher of the three races receives a medal at the finish. An individual ranking is drawn up for each race. Trophies and prizes are awarded to the top three senior and veteran men, and to the top three senior and veteran women in the scratch ranking, regardless of age category. No cash prize is awarded. The presence of the awarded participants is mandatory: in case of absence, the prizes remain with the organisation. Article 12 · Cancellation and refund On presentation of a medical certificate only, the organisation refunds 50% of the registration fee (excluding fees charged by njuko) up to one month before the event. No other reason gives rise to a refund, and no refund is possible in the month before the event. In the event of an exceptional cancellation for which the organisation is not responsible (force majeure, safety requirements, weather conditions, decision of the authorities, etc.), no registration can be refunded and no damages can be claimed. Article 13 · Race number transfer A race number transfer is possible until Thursday 1 April 2027 at 20:00, only between runners, via the njuko participant area (the "Transférer mon inscription" button). The new participant registers with payment; the registration is effective once payment has been made, and the participant who transferred their race number is refunded within 8 days. The organisation cannot carry out a transfer itself. Race numbers cannot be carried over to the following edition, except if the event is postponed. Article 14 · Sanctions Any participant caught throwing litter outside the designated areas, showing unsporting behaviour, disrespecting volunteers or failing to comply with these rules will be called to order, then disqualified in case of a repeat offence; they will then have to reach the finish by their own means. No claim will be accepted. Article 15 · Insurance and liability The organisation has taken out civil liability insurance. It is up to participants to insure themselves personally. The organisation cannot be held responsible in the event of an accident or failure of participants, in particular those resulting from poor health or insufficient preparation. Participation is under the full responsibility of competitors, with waiver of any recourse against the organisation in the event of damage or after-effects subsequent to the race. The organisation declines all responsibility in the event of theft or damage to equipment. Article 16 · Image rights and personal data Each participant authorises LIGHT ON to use images in which they may be identified, as part of promotional and advertising broadcasts. In accordance with the French Data Protection Act of 6 January 1978 and the GDPR, each participant has a right of access and rectification of their personal data, by writing to hello@lightontri.com. Information For any question about the races: hello@lightontri.com or +33 3 74 47 56 52. Race director: Julien Labdant.
